brief: a nick in one backbone of a DNA duplex closes: the two facing ends reach across the gap, meet in the middle and seal into one continuous unbroken strand, while everything else stays still
look: A short length of DNA drawn flat and side-on: a continuous blue template backbone along the bottom, an amber backbone above it, and between them one row of evenly spaced rungs at a single pitch, each rung two coloured halves meeting in the middle. The AMBER backbone alone is interrupted by one small clean gap near the centre — the nick. The blue template is unbroken, the rungs continue across the gap, and nothing else is in the picture.
